gaps.sentence: The company ___ losses of two million last year.
He ___ a speech at the wedding that moved everyone.
gaps.explanation: 'Make a speech' is the collocation; say/tell take different structures.

gaps.sentence: Their wedding ___ place on a remote island.
gaps.explanation: 'Take place' is the fixed phrase for events.

gaps.sentence: She ___ her breath before diving into the pool.
gaps.explanation: 'Hold one's breath' — catching breath is recovering it afterwards.

gaps.sentence: Her company ___ a huge profit last year.
gaps.explanation: make a profit (or make a loss) is the fixed business collocation.

gaps.sentence: I was nearly late, but I managed to ___ the last bus.
gaps.hint: to get on a bus or train in time
gaps.explanation: catch a bus/train means to arrive in time to board it; the words 'managed to' and 'nearly late' show success.

gaps.sentence: The judge ___ the verdict after four hours of deliberation.
gaps.explanation: 'Deliver a verdict/judgement' is the legal collocation.

gaps.sentence: The new CEO is keen to ___ her mark on the company.
gaps.hint: make your mark = have an impact
gaps.explanation: 'Make your mark on something' = have a clear, lasting effect on it.
